mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the enforcement that successful operations require an allowed role lets the model construct a Success operation whose caller's role set has no cell in the permission matrix for the op kind (e.g., an auditor-only user successfully POSTing).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation, u: User | op.caller = u and u.roles = AuditorRole and op.kind = PostApplications and op.outcome = Success and op.authenticated = BTrue }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the auth-before-business-logic fact lets the model invent an unauthenticated operation that nonetheless succeeds, which AuthRequiredEverywhere is meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthRequiredViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = BFalse and op.outcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit-completeness fact allows a successful state-changing operation to exist without a paired audit entry, which AuditCompleteness must flag.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and op.kind = PostApplications and no op.audit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Without the append-only fact, two distinct audit entries can record the same transition on the same application, which is exactly the duplication AppendOnly forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.application = ae2.application and ae1.prevStatus = ae2.prevStatus and ae1.newStatus = ae2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing no-self-assignment lets an application be assigned to its own applicant; combined with the assigned-officer-patches rule, this yields a successful PATCH where caller == applicant, violating no-self-mutation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoSelfAssignmentViolation { some app: LoanApplication, op: Operation | app.assignedOfficer = app.applicant and op.target = app and op.kind = PatchStatus and op.outcome = Success and op.caller = app.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the not-found-on-denial fact lets the model expose a Forbidden outcome for an authenticated GET denial, which leaks resource existence and is exactly what NoInformationLeakage forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoInformationLeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = BTrue and op.kind = GetApplicationById and op.outcome = Forbidden }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing ownership-gated read access lets a stranger (not applicant, not assigned officer, not auditor) successfully GET an application, which OwnershipBasedAccess must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBasedAccessViolation { some op: Operation, u: User | op.caller = u and op.kind = GetApplicationById and op.outcome = Success and u != op.target.applicant and u != op.target.assignedOfficer and AuditorRole not in u.roles }
